title: Islamic Banking vs Conventional Banking in Pakistan: Core Principles & Practical Differences
author: Dr. Tariq Mahmood
excerpt: Discover how Islamic banking operates without Riba (interest), exploring Diminishing Musharakah, Ijarah, and Murabaha compared to conventional fractional reserve banking in Pakistan.
content:
Understanding the Islamic Financial Paradigm

Pakistan has emerged as one of the world's most progressive jurisdictions for Islamic banking. Governed by strict regulations from the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) and supervised by the Federal Shariat Court's landmark directives, Islamic financial institutions have grown to capture over 20% of the country's total banking assets.

Unlike conventional banking, where money itself is treated as a commodity lent at a predetermined interest rate (Riba), Islamic finance is rooted in real asset backing, ethical risk-sharing, and prohibition of speculative uncertainty (Gharar).

Key Operational Mechanisms

  • Mudarabah (Profit-Sharing Partnership): Depositors act as Rabb-ul-Maal (capital providers) while the bank acts as Mudarib (investment manager). Profits generated from permissible investments are distributed according to an agreed profit-sharing ratio, while financial loss is borne by the capital provider.
  • Diminishing Musharakah: Widely employed for home financing (e.g., Meezan Easy Home), the bank and client jointly purchase an asset. The client pays rent for the bank's share while gradually purchasing ownership units until full title is transferred.
  • Ijarah Muntahia Bittamleek: The Islamic equivalent of auto leasing, where the bank maintains asset ownership and bears major maintenance/takaful risks throughout the rental period.

Conventional vs Islamic: Summary Comparison

In conventional lending, delayed payments result in compounding penalty interest that adds to the bank's revenue. In contrast, under Islamic banking rules, any late payment compensation charged to enforce discipline cannot become bank income; it is strictly directed to an audited Shariah charity fund.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Car Financing in Pakistan: Car Ijarah vs Auto Loan
author: Ayesha Bilal
excerpt: A step-by-step breakdown of automobile financing options in Pakistan, comparing KIBOR markups, Islamic Ijarah rental models, insurance/takaful costs, and down payment mandates.
content:
Navigating Auto Financing in Pakistan

Purchasing an automobile in Pakistan today represents a significant capital expenditure. Whether you are looking at locally assembled vehicles like the Suzuki Alto, Toyota Yaris, Honda City, or imported crossover SUVs, choosing between a conventional auto loan and an Islamic Car Ijarah can save you hundreds of thousands of rupees over your loan tenure.

SBP Prudential Regulations on Auto Loans

The State Bank of Pakistan regulates consumer auto lending strictly to control consumer demand and curb inflationary pressures:

  • Maximum Tenure: Capped at 5 years for locally assembled cars under 1,000cc, and 3 to 5 years for larger engine displacement vehicles.
  • Minimum Down Payment (Equity): Usually between 15% and 30% depending on engine capacity and vehicle type.
  • Debt Burden Ratio (DBR): Your total monthly debt obligations (including the car installment) must not exceed 40% of your verifiable net monthly income.

Car Ijarah vs Conventional Auto Loan

In a conventional auto loan (such as Bank Alfalah Auto Loan or HBL CarLoan), the vehicle is registered in the customer's name with an HPA (Hire Purchase Agreement) lien marked in favor of the bank. In an Islamic Car Ijarah (such as Meezan Car Ijarah or Dubai Islamic Bank), the car is owned by the bank and rented to you, meaning that ownership risks and total vehicle insurance/takaful responsibilities during total loss remain with the lessor.

title: SBP Raast & Instant Digital Payments: How Instant P2P and P2M Transactions Work
author: Khurram Shehzad
excerpt: Learn how the State Bank of Pakistan's Raast payment system provides zero-fee, instant person-to-person and merchant payments using mobile numbers.
content:
Pakistan's Digital Payments Revolution

Raast is Pakistan’s first instant payment system developed by the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) under the National Financial Inclusion Strategy. Raast operates 24/7/365, offering instantaneous settlement between banks, microfinance banks, and electronic money institutions (EMIs) with zero transaction fees.

How Raast ID Works

Previously, sending money required memorizing or copying a 24-digit International Bank Account Number (IBAN). Raast introduced Raast ID, which directly links your registered Pakistani mobile telephone number to your bank account.

Whenever someone wishes to send money to you, they only need your mobile phone number. The transaction clears in less than 3 seconds directly into your designated bank account.

Key Features of Raast

  • Zero Transfer Charges: Unlike legacy IBFT methods that occasionally levied transaction fees, Raast transfers are completely free for end users.
  • P2M Merchant QR Payments: Shopkeepers and retail outlets across Pakistan can now accept payments via standardized Raast QR codes without expensive POS card terminals.
  • Interoperability: Works seamlessly across conventional banks, Islamic banks, JazzCash, Nayapay, Sadapay, and Easypaisa.

title: A Complete Guide to Home Financing & Housing Schemes in Pakistan
author: Farhan Zafar
excerpt: Everything you need to know about purchasing or constructing a house in Pakistan through Diminishing Musharakah and conventional mortgage schemes.
content:
Making Home Ownership Achievable

Owning a home is one of the most cherished milestones for Pakistani families. In recent years, both private commercial banks and Islamic banks have expanded their housing finance portfolios, offering loans for home purchase, plot purchase plus construction, and home renovation.

Eligibility & Income Pooling

One of the most powerful features of modern housing finance in Pakistan is income pooling. If your individual salary does not meet the debt-burden ratio required for the target financing amount, banks allow you to co-apply with your spouse, parents, or employed siblings, combining your collective household income to qualify for a larger loan.

Property Due Diligence Requirements

Before disbursing any mortgage loan, the bank’s approved legal and property valuation panel conducts thorough checks:

  • Approved building plans from municipal authorities (e.g., LDA, KDA, CDA, DHA, Bahria).
  • Clear legal title and 30-year search report verifying no prior mortgages or encumbrances.
  • Independent property valuation to determine fair market value and forced sale value (FSV).

title: Credit Cards in Pakistan: Reward Points, Lounge Access, and Annual Fee Waivers
author: Sara Qureshi
excerpt: A comparative overview of premium credit cards in Pakistan, exploring dining discounts, CIP airport lounges, cashback perks, and annual fee waivers.
content:
Unlocking Value from Credit Cards

Credit cards in Pakistan have evolved from simple payment tools into comprehensive lifestyle accessories. With the right card, users can save tens of thousands of rupees annually through dining discounts, cashback, and airline loyalty miles.

Airport Lounge Privileges

Top-tier cards such as Bank Alfalah Premier, HBL World Elite, and Standard Chartered Priority Visa Infinite offer complimentary access to domestic CIP lounges in Karachi, Lahore, and Islamabad airports, as well as Priority Pass and LoungeKey access to over 1,200 international airport lounges worldwide.

Managing Annual Fees and Interest Rates

Most commercial banks charge an annual card membership fee ranging from PKR 5,000 to PKR 30,000 depending on the tier. However, virtually all banks offer annual fee reversals if you achieve a designated spending milestone within the first 60 days or across the billing year.

title: Roshan Digital Account (RDA): Features, Naya Pakistan Certificates, and Inward Remittance
author: Dr. Tariq Mahmood
excerpt: An exhaustive guide for Non-Resident Pakistanis (NRPs) on opening an RDA, investing in sovereign Naya Pakistan Certificates, and repatriating funds freely.
content:
Empowering Overseas Pakistanis

The Roshan Digital Account (RDA) is a transformative initiative by the State Bank of Pakistan together with major commercial and Islamic banks. RDA allows Non-Resident Pakistanis (NRPs) living anywhere in the world to open a bank account in Pakistan entirely online within 48 hours without visiting an embassy or bank branch.

Key Benefits of RDA

  • Full Repatriability: Funds remitted into an RDA can be remitted back overseas at any time without requiring prior approval from the State Bank of Pakistan.
  • Naya Pakistan Certificates (NPCs): Investors can purchase government-backed US Dollar, GBP, Euro, or PKR sovereign certificates offering highly competitive profit rates.
  • Roshan Apna Ghar & Roshan Apni Car: Overseas Pakistanis can finance property and brand-new cars for their families residing in Pakistan with streamlined documentation.
  • Roshan Equity Investment: Direct access to the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) to trade equities securely.
